analysis.reason: The paper reports the discovery and orbital/stellar characterization of SMASH J004005-733351 in the SMC, an intermediate-mass stripped star with a dark companion (minimum mass $M_2 \gtrsim 1.2\,M_\odot$, likely a neutron star). This system serves as a direct progenitor benchmark for stripped-envelope core-collapse supernovae (Type Ib/ultra-stripped SNe) and double neutron star mergers.
analysis.result: The binary has an orbital period of $P_{\rm orb} = 19.95 \pm 0.002\,{\rm hr}$ ($19.947 \pm 0.002\,{\rm hr}$), radial velocity semi-amplitude $K = 91.7^{+3.2}_{-3.1}\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}}$, and eccentricity $e = 0.032^{+0.031}_{-0.022}$, yielding a binary mass function $f_m \approx 0.066\,M_\odot$. The stripped star has an evolutionary mass $M_{\rm evol} = 3.840 \pm 0.535\,M_\odot$ ($M_{\rm stripped} = 3.84 \pm 0.54\,M_\odot$), $T_{\rm eff} = 68.3 \pm 6.4\,{\rm kK}$, $\log(g/[{\rm cm\,s^{-2}}]) = 4.76 \pm 0.12$, radius $R = 0.99 \pm 0.09\,R_\odot$, luminosity $\log(L/L_\odot) = 4.28 \pm 0.13$, and an anomalously high surface hydrogen mass fraction $X_{\rm H,s} = 0.625^{+0.012}_{-0.011}\,(\mathrm{stat}) \pm 0.035\,(\mathrm{sys})$. For $M_{\rm stripped} = 3.84\,M_\odot$, the companion's minimum mass is $M_2 = 1.19\,M_\odot$ ($i = 90^\circ$) with a median of $1.41\,M_\odot$. Optical light curve limits rule out main-sequence companions (which would produce reflection variability $\ge 10\%$ vs observed limit $\lesssim 1\%$), and X-ray non-detection sets $L_X \lesssim 9 \times 10^{33}\,{\rm erg\,s^{-1}}$ ($0.2-12\,{\rm keV}$), highly consistent with a neutron star companion.
analysis.problem: Intermediate-mass stripped stars ($M \approx 2-7\,M_\odot$) in compact orbits with compact objects are key theoretical evolutionary precursors to stripped/ultra-stripped core-collapse supernovae and double compact object mergers, yet observational identifications of such binaries remain exceedingly sparse.
analysis.method: Target selection via SMASH $u$-band excess, Gaia astrometric membership, and follow-up multi-epoch intermediate-resolution spectroscopy (MagE and GMOS-S). Radial velocities were obtained by cross-correlation $\chi^2$ minimization against non-LTE stripped-star synthetic spectra and fitted with The Joker and MCMC (`emcee`). Atmospheric and physical parameters were determined via joint SED and non-LTE spectral fitting combined with MESA stellar evolutionary models ($Z = 0.002$). Companion irradiation constraints were simulated with PHOEBE against 3860 epochs of OGLE $I$-band light curves, coupled with XMM-Newton flux limits and Bondi-Hoyle-Lyttleton accretion rate modeling.
assumptions: Bondi-Hoyle-Lyttleton accretion framework with radiative efficiency $\eta \approx 0.1$ for interpreting X-ray luminosity limits.
limits: Inclination angle $i$ is not directly measured, so a massive white dwarf companion ($M_2 \le 1.44\,M_\odot$) cannot be strictly ruled out on dynamics alone, though 87% of the isotropic companion mass distribution falls in the $1-3\,M_\odot$ neutron star regime.

Current stellar evolution models fail to simultaneously reproduce both the high effective temperature / compact radius ($T_{\rm eff} \approx 68\,{\rm kK}, R \approx 1\,R_\odot$) and the high envelope hydrogen abundance ($X_{\rm H,s} \approx 0.63$).

analysis.reason: The paper presents CROMA, a GPU-accelerated Fokker-Planck solver for post-processing cosmological MHD simulations along Lagrangian tracer particles, incorporating cosmic ray protons, secondary electrons/neutrinos/gamma-rays via pp collisions, stochastic re-acceleration, and synchrotron emission.
analysis.result: CROMA implements an implicit Chang-Cooper scheme solved via Parallel Cyclic Reduction (PCR) on GPUs, achieving a tridiagonal solve throughput saturating at $R_{\rm solve} \approx 10^{3}\ \mathrm{tracers\ s^{-1}}$ per MPI task, an end-to-end wall-clock throughput of $R_{\rm wall} \approx 400\ \mathrm{tracers\ s^{-1}}$ per task at $N_{\rm trc} \sim 10^6$ ($N_{\rm bin} = 128$), an acceleration factor of $\sim 10\times$ compared to 32 CPU cores, and a synchrotron emissivity computation speedup by a factor of $N_\theta \approx 10^3$ using precomputed tables.
analysis.problem: Cosmological fluid simulations cannot resolve the microphysical evolution of cosmic-ray energy spectra over millions of Lagrangian tracers due to the prohibitive computational cost of Fokker-Planck solvers on CPUs.
analysis.method: One-dimensional momentum Fokker-Planck equation $\frac{\partial\mathcal{N}(p)}{\partial t} = \frac{\partial}{\partial p}\left[D_{pp}\frac{\partial\mathcal{N}(p)}{\partial p}+\left(H(p,z(t))-\frac{2}{p}D_{pp}\right)\mathcal{N}(p)\right] - \frac{\mathcal{N}}{T(p)} + Q(p,z(t))$ discretized via the Chang-Cooper finite difference scheme; tridiagonal system solved on GPUs using the PCR algorithm with $\mathcal{O}(N_{\rm bin}\log_2 N_{\rm bin})$ complexity; hadronic secondary creation ($pp \to \pi^{\pm, 0}$) and precomputed 2D lookup tables for pitch-angle-integrated synchrotron emission $j_\nu(\nu_l, B)$.
citation_leads: CROMA: a GPU-accelerated Fokker–Planck solver for modeling non-thermal emission in post-processing cosmological simulations: “The code evolves CR proton and electron spectra along Lagrangian tracer trajectories”

CROMA: a GPU-accelerated Fokker–Planck solver for modeling non-thermal emission in post-processing cosmological simulations: “We present a new C/C++-based FP solver with GPU acceleration for post-processing particle-based outputs from cosmological MHD simulations.”
5.2 GPU acceleration performance: “In our test case with $N_{\rm bin}=128$, the throughput of the tridiagonal solver saturates at around $R_{\rm solve}\approx 10^{3}$ tracers s-1 per MPI task.”
Appendix B Accuracy of the synchrotron table: “The table interpolation method accelerates the calculation of the synchrotron emissivity by a factor of $N_{\theta}$, i.e., $\approx 10^{3}$.”
analysis.research_progress: Constructed an open, GPU-accelerated post-processing pipeline for cluster non-thermal emission that accelerates FP tridiagonal evolution by nearly two orders of magnitude per task over single CPU cores, enabling tracking of $\gtrsim 10^6$ tracers with secondary hadronic chains.

analysis.result: Simulated gravitational-wave signals from an equal-mass, nonspinning binary boson star merger prompt-collapse scenario scaled to total mass $M = 71.5 M_\odot$ at network signal-to-noise ratio $\rho_{\rm network} = 80.2$ pass the observational horizon area-law consistency test (inferring $\Delta A = (A_f - A_i)/A_f > 0$) with confidence between $80\%$ and $92\%$, despite the premerger components lacking event horizons.
analysis.problem: Current gravitational-wave tests of Hawking's horizon area theorem infer horizon areas indirectly through parameterized waveform models that assume Kerr black holes in vacuum general relativity, rendering the physical interpretation of passing such tests inherently model dependent.
analysis.method: An equal-mass boson star merger simulation (A17-d17 using GRChombo) is injected into simulated Advanced LIGO O4 noise. The waveform is divided into inspiral and ringdown portions; the inspiral is analyzed with the numerical relativity surrogate model NRSur7dq4 using TDInf, while the ringdown is analyzed with damped sinusoids matched to Kerr quasinormal modes using ringdown and qnm. Component and remnant parameters are converted to horizon areas via the Kerr formula $A = 8\pi M^2 (1 + \sqrt{1 - |\vec{\chi}|^2})$.

analysis.reason: The paper demonstrates the Angular Distribution Function (ADF) method for reconstructing very inclined air showers using raw radio antenna voltages, which directly supports the detection pipeline for ultra-high-energy cosmic rays and Earth-skimming tau neutrinos in GRAND.
analysis.result: On realistic GP300 simulations, the ADF reconstruction achieves an angular resolution better than $0.07^\circ$ and a primary energy resolution $<15\%$. Applied to raw ADC data from 65 deployed antennas of GRANDProto300, it successfully identified 51 high-quality cosmic-ray candidate events with an illustrative event showing reconstructed direction $\theta = 75.1^\circ \pm 0.03^\circ$, $\phi = 358.7^\circ \pm 0.02^\circ$, reduced $\chi^2_{\nu,\mathrm{ADF}} = 4.7$, and primary energy $E = 2.08 \times 10^{18}\text{ eV}$.
analysis.problem: Reconstructing the full geometry (shower axis and emission source) and primary energy of very inclined air showers with sub-degree accuracy in autonomous radio arrays without requiring full electric-field deconvolution.
analysis.method: The method first fits a spherical wavefront to trigger times to obtain the point-like emission origin $X_{\mathrm{source}}$, accounting for atmospheric refraction. analysis.reason: The paper presents a covariant microscopic framework beyond standard Fokker-Planck gradual shear acceleration in relativistic jets, revealing sub-diffusive momentum transport and spectral hardening relevant to cosmic-ray and high-energy particle acceleration in relativistic transient outflows.
analysis.result: Particle shear acceleration in inhomogeneous relativistic velocity fields is governed by the effective shear tensor $\sigma(x) = \tilde{\sigma}/\gamma_{\rm J}$, which decreases in highly relativistic regions. analysis.problem: Standard Fokker-Planck transport models of shear acceleration assume gradual acceleration ($\tau' \sigma \ll 1$) with small momentum increments per scattering and often approximate the shear rate as spatially constant, which fails when particle mean free paths become comparable to the shear gradient scale or across relativistic velocity jumps.
analysis.method: A covariant stochastic differential equation (SDE) formulation based on the generalized Fermi acceleration framework tracking comoving momentum $p'$ and directional cosines $\mu_i'$, where pitch-angle scattering is implemented via an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process with scattering frequency $\nu' = 1/\tau'$ and validated against continuous-time random walk (CTRW) models.

analysis.reason: This work presents a comprehensive 55-year timing analysis of the 35-day super-orbital cycle of the accreting neutron star Hercules X-1, establishing fundamental observational constraints on tilted/warped accretion disk precession and compact object high-energy phenomenology.
analysis.result: Turn-Ons preferentially occur at binary orbital phases $\Phi_{\rm orb} \sim 0.25$ and $\sim 0.75$, with quantized cycle durations concentrated at $20.0$, $20.5$ (accounting for $\sim 57\%$), and $21.0 \times P_{\rm orb}$ ($P_{\rm orb} = 1.70016759\,\mathrm{d}$). The long-term $(O-C)$ timing residual curve reveals two distinct parabolic segments separated by Anomalous Low 3 (AL3): pre-AL3 has $P = 34.95\,\mathrm{d}$ and $\mathrm{d}P/\mathrm{d}t = (-1.8 \pm 0.2) \times 10^{-5}\,\mathrm{s\,s^{-1}}$, while post-AL3 has $P = 35.03\,\mathrm{d}$ and $\mathrm{d}P/\mathrm{d}t = (-5.30 \pm 0.23) \times 10^{-5}\,\mathrm{s\,s^{-1}}$. analysis.method:

analysis.reason: This paper presents a computational proof of concept reformulating gamma-ray point source detection into a QUBO problem for simulated quantum annealing, without addressing transient astrophysics, compact object physics, or relativistic jets.
analysis.result: The QUBO framework correctly identifies the true candidate grid position in $97\%$ of the $500$ simulated AGILE maps (with remaining cases displaced by $0.5^{\circ}$). The source flux is recovered with a mean bias of $-1.9\%$ (standard deviation $8.3\%$), while the isotropic normalization is biased low by $-20.0\%$ (standard deviation $10.8\%$). The resulting detection significance $\sqrt{\mathrm{TS}}$ spans $17$ to $145$ (mean $65$) and correlates strongly with classical values (Pearson $r = 0.997$).
analysis.problem: Classical maximum-likelihood estimation for gamma-ray source detection and localization optimizes continuous parameters over Poisson counts $\ln L = \sum_{ij} n_{ij}\ln(\theta_{ij}) - \sum_{ij}\theta_{ij}$, which is non-polynomial and incompatible with Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) architectures.
analysis.method: The authors adopt a Gaussian approximation to map the Poisson log-likelihood to an unweighted least-squares objective $\chi^{2} = \|Rx - d\|^{2} = x^{T}Wx - 2V^{T}x + d\cdot d$, discretize continuous parameters $x = (g_{b}, c_{a})^{T}$ via a fixed-point binary expansion $x_{i} = \beta \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} 2^{k} q_{k}$ with $n=12$ bits, and implement position selection across $M = 81$ grid candidates with a one-hot penalty $\lambda (\sum_{m=1}^{M} z_{m} - 1)^{2}$ solved via simulated quantum annealing (SQA).
assumptions: A single point source is located at high Galactic latitude ($b = 30^{\circ}$) where Galactic diffuse emission $G_{ij}$ is negligible.
limits: The formulation is restricted to a single point source, exhibits a systematic $-20.0\%$ bias in background normalization, and requires minor-embedding qubit counts that currently exceed physical quantum hardware.

analysis.reason: The paper presents a quantitative gravitational self-lensing scenario in BH-NS binaries driven by Lense-Thirring precession to explain periodically repeating FRBs and pulse energy magnification. It derives critical constraints on intermediate-mass black hole (IMBH) companions and pulse delay timescales directly relevant to FRB burst morphology and environmental modeling.
analysis.result: Pure Keplerian self-lensing fails with a tiny activity window $\tau_{\mathrm{aw}}^{\mathrm{KP}} \sim \mathcal{O}(0.5\,\mathrm{hours})$, whereas Lense-Thirring precession with period $\tau_{\mathrm{LT}} = \frac{\pi(1-e^{2})^{3/2}c^{3}a^{3}}{G^{2}M_{\mathrm{BH}}^{2}\chi} = 2\tau_{\mathrm{FRB}}$ reproduces wide activity windows $\tau_{\mathrm{aw}}^{\mathrm{LT}} \sim 0.5\tau_{\mathrm{FRB}}$ for small inclinations $i \sim (5\text{--}8) \times 10^{-2}\,{^\circ}$. Splitting time delays $\tau_{\mathrm{lens}}^{\mathrm{Spl}} \approx \frac{4GM_{\mathrm{BH}}}{c^3}(1+z)\lambda(r_s/a)^{1/2} \sim 10^{-3}\text{--}10^{-2}\,\mathrm{s}$ match the observed millisecond waiting-time peak in FRB 20121102A, constraining the companion mass to $M_{\mathrm{BH}} \sim 10^3\text{--}10^4\,M_\odot$ with maximum amplification $\mathcal{A}_{\max} \approx \sqrt{8r_{s}a/R^{2}} \sim 10^4$ and gravitational wave merger timescale $\tau_{\mathrm{GW}} \sim 10^3\,\mathrm{yr}$.
analysis.problem: Periodically repeating Fast Radio Bursts (prFRBs) exhibit broad periodic activity windows ($30\%\text{--}50\%$ of their period) and pulse energies orders of magnitude higher than Galactic magnetars, which existing free-precession, stellar-wind eclipse, or simple orbital models struggle to simultaneously explain.
analysis.method: The authors construct a post-Newtonian binary dynamics and gravitational self-lensing framework using the Maeder-Liebes finite-source weak-field approximation $L_{\rm Lensed} = g^4 \mathcal{A} L_{\rm NS}$, incorporating Lense-Thirring and pericenter precession $\langle d\Omega/dt \rangle = \frac{2G^2 M_{\rm BH}^2}{c^3 a^3 (1-e^2)^{3/2}} \chi$, relativistic timing delays (Rømer, Einstein, and Shapiro), and Monte Carlo simulations of magnetar-like log-normal pulse distributions.
assumptions: The radio emitter is a neutron star (or magnetar) in a close orbit around a rotating black hole, periodically emitting pulses with an intrinsic log-normal energy distribution.
limits: Standard Galactic magnetar intrinsic pulse energies ($10^{29}\text{--}10^{30}\,\mathrm{erg}$) require either an intrinsically brighter emitter ($\sim 10^{34}\,\mathrm{erg}$) or extremely small emission radii to reach the highest FRB energetics through weak lensing.

The population rate is highly constrained by the edge-on geometric alignment fraction $f_{\rm geom} \sim 10^{-3}$ and tight binary formation fractions, yielding $N_{\rm obs} \lesssim 1$, meaning this mechanism can only account for a rare subset of prFRBs rather than the broader FRB population.

analysis.reason: The paper presents a comprehensive X-ray spectral and timing analysis of 85 TeV blazars using Swift-XRT and NuSTAR data, investigating relativistic jet emission mechanisms and disk-jet coupling.
analysis.result: Luminosity correlations show $\log L_{\rm TeV}$ correlates positively with soft X-ray luminosity ($k = 1.54 \pm 0.20$, $r = 0.63$) and hard X-ray luminosity ($k = 1.23 \pm 0.28$, $r = 0.52$), consistent with leptonic scenarios. X-ray luminosity correlates strongly with disk luminosity $\log L_{\rm disk}$ ($r = 0.61$ soft, $r = 0.77$ hard) but lacks significant correlation with black hole mass $\log M_{\rm BH}$ ($p=0.21$ and $0.77$). analysis.problem: Unraveling the relativistic jet particle acceleration and emission mechanisms (leptonic vs hadronic processes) and understanding how central engine properties ($M_{\rm BH}$, $L_{\rm disk}$) regulate high-energy emission in TeV blazars.

analysis.result: The review synthesizes constraints on new physics across stellar laboratories, transient photon propagation, and neutrino telescopes. source_sections: Coherent Radio Emission from Flux Rope Mergers in 3D Relativistic Reconnection

analysis.reason: This work presents 3D PIC simulations of coherent radio emission from flux rope mergers in relativistic reconnection with outflow boundary conditions and guide fields, directly testing FRB and pulsar emission engine models.
analysis.result: Coherent fast magnetosonic waves are stably excited via flux rope mergers in 3D relativistic reconnection, yielding a radiation efficiency of $\eta \sim 7 \times 10^{-4}$ for $B_g/B_0 = 0$ and $\eta \sim (1\text{--}2) \times 10^{-3}$ for moderate guide fields ($B_g/B_0 = 0.1\text{--}0.3$). The escaping radiation is 100% linearly polarized X-mode ($\,\delta\bm{E}\perp\bm{B}$), with a polarization angle offset between opposite sides of the sheet of $\Delta\mathrm{PA} \sim 2\arctan(B_g/B_0)$.
analysis.problem: Whether 3D relativistic instabilities (e.g., relativistic drift kink instability and flux rope kink instability) and realistic outflow boundaries suppress coherent radio wave emission found in simplified 2D periodic relativistic reconnection simulations.
analysis.method: 3D particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations of pair plasmas using TRISTAN-MP with open outflow boundaries along $x$ ($L_x=1600\,c/\omega_p$, $L_z=816\,c/\omega_p$), cold magnetization $\sigma = B_0^2/(4\pi n_0 m c^2) = 10$, and guide fields $B_g/B_0 \in \{0, 0.1, 0.3\}$, diagnosing wave Poynting flux $S_{\mathrm{wave}}=(c/4\pi)(\delta E_{z}\delta B_{x}-\delta E_{x}\delta B_{z})$ and efficiency $\eta \equiv S_{\mathrm{wave}}/S_0$.
citation_leads: Coherent Radio Emission from Flux Rope Mergers in 3D Relativistic Reconnection: “We find $\eta\sim 7\times 10^{-4}$ without a guide field, a factor of a few below 2D results, and $\eta\sim(1\text{--}2)\times 10^{-3}$ at moderate guide fields, comparable to 2D with no guide field.”
III.1 Efficiency: “The efficiency of converting inflowing Poynting flux into outgoing coherent waves is thus”

III.3 Polarization angle: “In all our simulations, we find that these waves are linearly polarized X-mode waves (i.e., with $\delta\bm{E}\perp\bm{B}$), which, as we will show below, sets their polarization angle directly.”

IV Summary and Observational Implications: “In the presence of a guide field, waves escaping from opposite sides of the sheet therefore differ in PA by $\Delta\mathrm{PA}\sim 2\,\arctan(B_{g}/B_{0})$.”
analysis.research_progress: Demonstrates that 3D kinetic reconnection maintains high coherent emission efficiency $\eta \sim (1\text{--}2)\times 10^{-3}$ through interlocked flux rope structures, confirming reconnection as a viable coherent radio mechanism for FRBs and pulsar nanoshots.

figures.caption: Figure 4: Large-scale, coherent structures in the $B_{g}/B_{0}=0.3$ simulation at $ct/L=6.75$. Top row: Volume rendering of the average particle outflow velocity $\langle v_{x}\rangle/c$. Purple and red field lines show the upstream field above and below the sheet, respectively, and the tubes on each side of the sheet follow the corresponding field direction. The left panels zoom in on the interface between a tube above and a tube below the sheet, with a sample of reconnected field lines overlaid. The green and gold field lines originate from two different diffusion regions (shown in black, i.e., regions of strong $E_{\parallel})$, and are pulled in opposite directions along $x$. Both of these bundles of field lines cross the sheet, with one end above it and one end below it. Bottom row: Same as above, but showing particle density. The linkage point between the two bundles appears in the left-hand zoom-in as a large overdense region. The diffusion region that produced the green bundle is indicated by a black-outlined arrow, while a newly created flux rope is indicated by a purple-outlined arrow. A green bar indicates that the density structure is $\sim 200\,c/\omega_{p}$ wide.
figures.label: Fig. 4
figures.physical_core: The figure shows how reconnected field bundles from different diffusion regions are pulled in opposite directions along $x$, link across the current sheet, and form a large overdense structure. It illustrates the proposed physical picture for transporting reconnected field away from the diffusion regions in 3D.

figures.caption: Figure 5: Polarization angle (PA) of the outgoing waves, for $B_{g}/B_{0}=0$ (top row) and $B_{g}/B_{0}=0.3$ (bottom row), at $ct/L=5.6$. The four plots show $x$ – $z$ slices near the top of the box (left column) and bottom of the box (right column), $\sim 640\,c/\omega_{p}$ from the current sheet, showing the outgoing Poynting flux carried by the coherent waves, normalized by the inflowing flux $S_{0}$. The yellow-purple areas are patches of high-intensity waves. The light blue ticks denote the direction of the oscillating electric vector in these bright patches, whose angle from the $z$ axis is the PA. In the $B_{g}/B_{0}=0$ case, the waves escaping on either side of the box have their electric field aligned with the $z$ axis. For the $B_{g}/B_{0}=0.3$ case, on the other hand, because the PA of the outgoing waves is set by the direction of the upstream field, there is a rotation across the sheet by $\Delta\mathrm{PA}\sim 2\,\arctan(B_{g}/B_{0})$.
figures.label: Fig. 5
figures.physical_core: The simulated outgoing coherent waves are linearly polarized. Their polarization angle follows the upstream field direction; for $B_g/B_0=0.3$, the predicted rotation between waves escaping from opposite sides is $\Delta\mathrm{PA}\sim 2\arctan(B_g/B_0)$.

analysis.reason: This paper presents a systematic eROSITA eRASS1 survey of Galactic Be X-ray binaries in quiescence, providing valuable observational constraints on low-accretion-rate neutron star regimes relevant to compact object high-energy studies.
analysis.result: Detections in the $0.5-10\ \mathrm{keV}$ range reveal quiescent X-ray luminosities spanning $L_{\mathrm{X}} \sim 10^{33}-10^{36}\ \mathrm{erg\ s^{-1}}$, with photon indices $\Gamma \sim 0.5-2.0$ and blackbody temperatures $kT_{\rm bb} \sim 0.8-1.6\ \mathrm{keV}$ from emitting radii $R \sim 0.1-2\ \mathrm{km}$. A power-law correlation connects X-ray luminosity and emission radius as $L \propto R^{\alpha}$ with index $\alpha = 2.3 \pm 0.2$. In addition, upper limits on non-detected sources (e.g. 2S 1553$-$542 and RX J0812.4$-$3114) fall below the theoretical propeller luminosity $L_{\rm prop} \simeq 4\times 10^{37}k^{7/2}B_{12}^{2}P^{-7/3}M_{1.4}^{-2/3}R_{6}^{5}\ \mathrm{erg\ s^{-1}}$, confirming propeller or cold disc inhibition.

analysis.problem: Determining the accretion mechanisms and emission states (such as the propeller phase, cold disc accretion, or deep crustal heating) governing neutron star Be X-ray binaries at very low mass-transfer rates during quiescence.
analysis.method: Analysis of SRG/eROSITA eRASS1 survey data ($0.2-8\ \mathrm{keV}$) using Cash statistics and Akaike Information Criterion ($\mathrm{AIC} = 2k + C$) in XSPEC to fit absorbed power-law (`tbabs*powerlaw`) and absorbed blackbody (`tbabs*bbodyrad`) models, compared against theoretical thresholds for propeller transitions ($L_{\rm prop}$) and cold disk accretion ($L_{\rm cold}$).

Colour encodes the measured photon index on the diverging scale shown at the bottom, which is centred on $\Gamma=2.1$, the middle of the transition region; blue corresponds to hard, BL Lac-like spectra and red to soft, FSRQ-like spectra. Rows are ordered by mean photon index within each group, so that the progression from hard to soft spectra can be followed down the panel. The control rows provide a visual reference: a source of stable spectral type appears as a row of nearly uniform colour, so departures from uniformity in the CLB rows can be judged against sources of known classification rather than in isolation. Control sources can depart from the colour typical of their class: 4FGL J1229.0 $+$ 0202 (3C 273) is uniformly soft, while 4FGL J0957.6 $+$ 5523 (4C $+$ 55.17) appears predominantly hard and has had its FSRQ classification questioned ( McConville et al., 2011 ).

analysis.reason: The paper investigates the equation of state and structure of hot, lepton-rich proto-neutron stars and merger remnants with two-flavor color-superconducting quark matter, demonstrating that neutrino trapping delays quark deconfinement to higher baryon densities and strongly suppresses the sensitivity to the nuclear symmetry energy slope.
analysis.result: Neutrino trapping ($Y_{Le}=0.4$) robustly shifts the hadron-quark deconfinement transition toward higher baryon densities compared to neutrino-transparent matter. Trapping raises the proton fraction and diminishes the isospin asymmetry $\delta = 1-2Y_p$, which sharply reduces the equation of state's sensitivity to the hadronic symmetry energy slope ($L_{\rm sym} \in [30, 70]~\mathrm{MeV}$) because symmetry-energy energy density scales as $\propto E_{\rm sym}(\varrho)\,\delta^2$. For the reference DDLS50-NJL model ($\eta_D = \eta_V = 1$), maximum gravitational masses are $M_{\max}^{(S=1)} = 2.36\,M_\odot$ and $M_{\max}^{(S=2)} = 2.37\,M_\odot$; varying the vector coupling $\eta_V = G_V/G_S \in [0.8, 1.2]$ alters $M_{\max}$ by $\pm 1.3\%$, while strong diquark pairing ($\eta_D = 1.25$) reduces $M_{\max}$ by up to $-8.5\%$. While Gibbs (global lepton conservation) and Maxwell (local lepton conservation) phase constructions produce nearly indistinguishable macroscopical $M-R$ curves, Gibbs produces a vastly more extended geometric radial mixed-phase core.
analysis.problem: How neutrino trapping, diquark pairing (2SC phase), vector repulsion, and phase equilibrium construction (Gibbs vs. Maxwell) affect the equation of state, deconfinement density, and structural profiles of proto-neutron stars and post-merger remnants across nuclear symmetry energy uncertainties.

analysis.reason: The paper presents the first large, statistical sample of 236 extreme scattering events (ESEs) from the ASKAP VAST survey, expanding the historical sample by more than a factor of five. This provides key constraints on AU-scale ionized plasma structures, overpressure states in the ISM, and the propagation environments of compact radio transients.
analysis.result: The authors identify 236 ESE candidates (72 gold, 76 silver, 88 bronze) with flux variations $\ge 2$. Under a characteristic scale $a \approx 1\;\mathrm{AU}$ and scale height $\approx 1\;\mathrm{kpc}$, the inferred core electron density is $n_0 \gtrsim 100\;\mathrm{cm^{-3}}$, implying an overpressured plasma lens with $P/k > 10^2 T_e\;\mathrm{K\,cm^{-3}}$. The measured ESE event rates at $888\;\mathrm{MHz}$ over a $12,500\;\mathrm{deg^2}$ footprint are $0.003\;(0.006)\;\mathrm{events/source/year}$ and $0.006\;(0.012)\;\mathrm{events/year/deg^2}$ for the gold (gold+silver) samples, with light curves strongly favoring overdense lenses ($\alpha > 0$).
analysis.problem: Extreme scattering events (ESEs) are probe tools for $\sim\mathrm{AU}$-scale interstellar medium structures, but historically only $\sim 30$ events were known over four decades. Determining their true spatial distribution, event rates, density profiles (overdense vs underdense), and resolving the extreme overpressure crisis in the warm ionized medium have remained unconstrained due to small sample sizes.
analysis.method: Candidates were selected from 24,590 bright compact sources in the ASKAP VAST $888\;\mathrm{MHz}$ survey using flux variation ratio $\ge 2$, ML filtering, comparison with VLASS $3\;\mathrm{GHz}$, and dynamic spectrum evolution ($S_\nu \propto \nu^\alpha$). analysis.reason: This paper investigates whether electron-capture supernovae (ECSNe) coupled with circumstellar dust attenuation and CSM interaction can account for intermediate-luminosity red transients (ILRTs), which directly connects to CSM interaction and supernova plateau physics.
analysis.result: Standard ECSN models with dusty winds cannot simultaneously reproduce the light curves and colors of ILRTs: the intrinsic drop in input luminosity after the plateau causes $r_{\rm sub} \propto L_{\rm input}^{1/2}$ to shrink, triggering a runaway increase in optical depth $\tau_V$ and causing the optical luminosity to plummet by orders of magnitude; attempting to flatten the decline using dense CSM shock interaction ($L_{s,\rm rad} \propto t^{-0.3}$) requires $\dot{M}_{\rm dense} \simeq 9.7 \times 10^{-3}\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$ and produces excessively red post-plateau colors ($B - V > 4$) that contradict observed ILRT colors ($B - V \lesssim 1.2\text{--}1.6$).
analysis.problem: Theoretical ECSN models from super-AGB progenitors predict plateau luminosities ($10^{41}\text{--}10^{42}\text{ erg s}^{-1}$) and post-plateau drops that are too luminous and steep compared to smooth, low-luminosity ILRTs like SN 2008S and NGC 300-OT.
analysis.method: The authors develop a semi-analytical radiative transfer framework coupling ECSN light curves with Chevalier-type shock interaction luminosity ($L_s(t) \simeq \frac{1}{2}\dot{M} v_s^3 / v_w \propto t^{-0.3}$), amorphous carbon dust grain growth limited by gas recombination and growth timescales ($f_{\rm dust}(r,t)$), dynamic dust sublimation ($r_{\rm sub} \propto L_{\rm input}^{1/2}$), and light-travel time boxcar smoothing ($2R/c$).
citation_leads: 4.1. Comparison to ILRT light curves: “The combination of the intrinsic sharp drop in $L _ { \mathrm { i n p u t } }$ and the sharply rising τV results in the optical luminosity plummeting by orders of magnitude.”

3.2. Dust Formation and Growth: “Even if the above condition on dust formation is met at a given radii, build-up of dust is gradual. Kochanek (2011) identifies the bottlenecks to be the recombination of gas ionized by the shock breakout, and the growth of the dust grains.”
4.2. Increase in shock luminosity: “We find that models with large $\dot { M } _ { - 4 }$ in order to match the plateau luminosity results in extremely red colors (large $B - V )$ after the plateau.”
analysis.research_progress: Demonstrates that fine-tuning dust extinction and CSM shock luminosity in canonical ECSN explosions ($E_{\rm ej} \sim 10^{50}\text{ erg}$) fails to match ILRT observations due to severe dust reddening ($B - V > 4$), indicating that ILRTs likely originate from inherently lower-energy explosions ($10^{48}\text{--}10^{49}\text{ erg}$) such as thermonuclear ECSNe or accretion-induced collapse.

analysis.reason: The paper reports the discovery and orbital/stellar characterization of SMASH J004005-733351 in the SMC, an intermediate-mass stripped star with a dark companion (minimum mass $M_2 \gtrsim 1.2\,M_\odot$, likely a neutron star). This system serves as a direct progenitor benchmark for stripped-envelope core-collapse supernovae (Type Ib/ultra-stripped SNe) and double neutron star mergers.
analysis.result: The binary has an orbital period of $P_{\rm orb} = 19.95 \pm 0.002\,{\rm hr}$ ($19.947 \pm 0.002\,{\rm hr}$), radial velocity semi-amplitude $K = 91.7^{+3.2}_{-3.1}\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}}$, and eccentricity $e = 0.032^{+0.031}_{-0.022}$, yielding a binary mass function $f_m \approx 0.066\,M_\odot$. The stripped star has an evolutionary mass $M_{\rm evol} = 3.840 \pm 0.535\,M_\odot$ ($M_{\rm stripped} = 3.84 \pm 0.54\,M_\odot$), $T_{\rm eff} = 68.3 \pm 6.4\,{\rm kK}$, $\log(g/[{\rm cm\,s^{-2}}]) = 4.76 \pm 0.12$, radius $R = 0.99 \pm 0.09\,R_\odot$, luminosity $\log(L/L_\odot) = 4.28 \pm 0.13$, and an anomalously high surface hydrogen mass fraction $X_{\rm H,s} = 0.625^{+0.012}_{-0.011}\,(\mathrm{stat}) \pm 0.035\,(\mathrm{sys})$. For $M_{\rm stripped} = 3.84\,M_\odot$, the companion's minimum mass is $M_2 = 1.19\,M_\odot$ ($i = 90^\circ$) with a median of $1.41\,M_\odot$. Optical light curve limits rule out main-sequence companions (which would produce reflection variability $\ge 10\%$ vs observed limit $\lesssim 1\%$), and X-ray non-detection sets $L_X \lesssim 9 \times 10^{33}\,{\rm erg\,s^{-1}}$ ($0.2-12\,{\rm keV}$), highly consistent with a neutron star companion.
analysis.problem: Intermediate-mass stripped stars ($M \approx 2-7\,M_\odot$) in compact orbits with compact objects are key theoretical evolutionary precursors to stripped/ultra-stripped core-collapse supernovae and double compact object mergers, yet observational identifications of such binaries remain exceedingly sparse.
analysis.method: Target selection via SMASH $u$-band excess, Gaia astrometric membership, and follow-up multi-epoch intermediate-resolution spectroscopy (MagE and GMOS-S). Radial velocities were obtained by cross-correlation $\chi^2$ minimization against non-LTE stripped-star synthetic spectra and fitted with The Joker and MCMC (`emcee`). Atmospheric and physical parameters were determined via joint SED and non-LTE spectral fitting combined with MESA stellar evolutionary models ($Z = 0.002$). Companion irradiation constraints were simulated with PHOEBE against 3860 epochs of OGLE $I$-band light curves, coupled with XMM-Newton flux limits and Bondi-Hoyle-Lyttleton accretion rate modeling.
assumptions: Bondi-Hoyle-Lyttleton accretion framework with radiative efficiency $\eta \approx 0.1$ for interpreting X-ray luminosity limits.
limits: Inclination angle $i$ is not directly measured, so a massive white dwarf companion ($M_2 \le 1.44\,M_\odot$) cannot be strictly ruled out on dynamics alone, though 87% of the isotropic companion mass distribution falls in the $1-3\,M_\odot$ neutron star regime.

The waveform is divided into inspiral and ringdown portions; the inspiral is analyzed with the numerical relativity surrogate model NRSur7dq4 using TDInf, while the ringdown is analyzed with damped sinusoids matched to Kerr quasinormal modes using ringdown and qnm. Component and remnant parameters are converted to horizon areas via the Kerr formula $A = 8\pi M^2 (1 + \sqrt{1 - |\vec{\chi}|^2})$.

analysis.method: The method first fits a spherical wavefront to trigger times to obtain the point-like emission origin $X_{\mathrm{source}}$, accounting for atmospheric refraction. analysis.problem: Previous simulations of neutron-star merger remnants commonly adopted effective two-flavor approximations (assuming indistinguishable $\nu_\mu$ and $\nu_\tau$) and phenomenological subgrid models, which fail to capture the impact of muonization physics and three-flavor non-linear quantum kinetic coherence on flavor instability criteria.
analysis.method:
Hydrodynamical profiles from a 3D general relativistic M1 merger simulation ($2.5\,M_\odot$ remnant at $ ar{t} \simeq 30\,\mathrm{ms}$) are mapped into the axisymmetric GR Boltzmann solver Gmunu coupled with the Weakhub reaction library. The framework solves the six-dimensional Boltzmann equation for all six neutrino species ($npe\mu$ matter) incorporating complete muonic charged- and neutral-current reactions, regularized in the dilute-muon limit via a Broyden-based nested implicit solver. limits: Detection and spatial distribution of fast flavor instabilities exhibit severe resolution dependence, where insufficient spatial and momentum angular grid resolutions substantially underestimate FFI occurrences.

analysis.result: Systematic sine-wave fits to radio monitoring light curves demonstrate robust 2:1 period commensurabilities in SMBHB candidates PKS J0805$-$0111, PKS J1309+1154, and PKS 2131$-$021, where subtracting fundamental and harmonic modes reduces residual variance by 50%–65% and 20%–44%, respectively. For secondary companion-induced modulation, orbital radius and velocity scale as $r/10^{16}\,{\rm cm} \sim 1.5 P_y^{2/3} M_{P9}^{1/3}$ and $v/10^9\,{\rm cm\,s^{-1}} \sim 3 P_y^{-1/3} M_{P9}^{1/3}$, balancing the disk wind magnetic pressure $B_W \sim L_{j\,44}^{1/2} r_{16}^{-1}\,{\rm G}$ at $r_*/r \sim 0.2 L_{j44}^{1/2} M_{P9}^{1/3} P_y^{-1/3}$.

analysis.reason: The paper presents a covariant microscopic framework beyond standard Fokker-Planck gradual shear acceleration in relativistic jets, revealing sub-diffusive momentum transport and spectral hardening relevant to cosmic-ray and high-energy particle acceleration in relativistic transient outflows.
analysis.result: Particle shear acceleration in inhomogeneous relativistic velocity fields is governed by the effective shear tensor $\sigma(x) = \tilde{\sigma}/\gamma_{\rm J}$, which decreases in highly relativistic regions. When $\sigma \tau' \gtrsim 1$, the return time distribution between crossing events exhibits a heavy-tailed power-law $p(t_{\rm cross}) \propto t_{\rm cross}^{-1.27}$, driving sub-diffusive momentum gain ($\langle p^{\prime 2}\rangle \propto t^q, q < 1$) and causing a spectral transition/hardening at $\sigma \tau'(p') \sim 1$ from gradual shear ($n(p') \propto p'^{-2}$ for $\delta=1$) to an intermittent non-gradual acceleration branch.
analysis.problem: Standard Fokker-Planck transport models of shear acceleration assume gradual acceleration ($\tau' \sigma \ll 1$) with small momentum increments per scattering and often approximate the shear rate as spatially constant, which fails when particle mean free paths become comparable to the shear gradient scale or across relativistic velocity jumps.
analysis.method: A covariant stochastic differential equation (SDE) formulation based on the generalized Fermi acceleration framework tracking comoving momentum $p'$ and directional cosines $\mu_i'$, where pitch-angle scattering is implemented via an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process with scattering frequency $\nu' = 1/\tau'$ and validated against continuous-time random walk (CTRW) models.
citation_leads: I Introduction: “Being covariant and non-perturbative by construction, this approach remains valid beyond the realm of the Fokker-Planck approximation”
II Generalized Fermi Model: “A key observation is that $\sigma$ decreases in regions where the flow becomes relativistic, because $\sigma=\tilde{\sigma}/\gamma_{\rm J}$.”

III.3 Towards non-gradual shear acceleration: $sigmatau^primegtrsim 1$: “This distribution $p(t_{\rm cross})$ exhibits a tail $\propto t_{\rm cross}^{-1.27}$, which implies that the mean waiting time is not well defined, and that the random walk in momentum must be sub-diffusive.”
IV.2 Momentum-dependent scattering time: “Thus, a momentum-dependent mean free path can imprint a spectral feature at the momentum for which $\sigma\tau^{\prime}(p^{\prime})\sim 1$.”

V Summary: “If $\tau^{\prime}$ increases with momentum, the parameter $\sigma\tau^{\prime}$ grows during acceleration, so that a particle population can move from the gradual regime to an intermittent, non-gradual regime.”
analysis.research_progress: Demonstrated that shear acceleration in relativistic jets is inherently non-local: high $\gamma_{\rm J}$ suppresses lab-frame transverse velocity by $1/\gamma_{\rm J}$, inducing heavy-tailed return times $p(t_{\rm cross}) \propto t_{\rm cross}^{-1.27}$ that transform momentum diffusion into a sub-diffusive regime and imprint a characteristic spectral break at $\sigma \tau'(p') \sim 1$.

analysis.reason: This work presents a comprehensive 55-year timing analysis of the 35-day super-orbital cycle of the accreting neutron star Hercules X-1, establishing fundamental observational constraints on tilted/warped accretion disk precession and compact object high-energy phenomenology.
analysis.result: Turn-Ons preferentially occur at binary orbital phases $\Phi_{\rm orb} \sim 0.25$ and $\sim 0.75$, with quantized cycle durations concentrated at $20.0$, $20.5$ (accounting for $\sim 57\%$), and $21.0 \times P_{\rm orb}$ ($P_{\rm orb} = 1.70016759\,\mathrm{d}$). The long-term $(O-C)$ timing residual curve reveals two distinct parabolic segments separated by Anomalous Low 3 (AL3): pre-AL3 has $P = 34.95\,\mathrm{d}$ and $\mathrm{d}P/\mathrm{d}t = (-1.8 \pm 0.2) \times 10^{-5}\,\mathrm{s\,s^{-1}}$, while post-AL3 has $P = 35.03\,\mathrm{d}$ and $\mathrm{d}P/\mathrm{d}t = (-5.30 \pm 0.23) \times 10^{-5}\,\mathrm{s\,s^{-1}}$. Anomalous Lows recur with a mean period of $(5.35 \pm 0.03)\,\mathrm{yr}$.
analysis.problem: Unraveling the timing regularity, quantized phase transitions, and physical drivers behind the irregular $\sim 35\,\mathrm{d}$ super-orbital clock and quasi-periodic Anomalous Lows in Her X-1 over multi-decade baselines.
analysis.method:
Compiled and analyzed 55 years of X-ray monitoring data across 570 cycles (UHURU to Swift/BAT, MAXI, and Fermi/GBM). Turn-On is formally defined as the time when X-ray flux reaches $30\%$ of the subsequent Main-On peak flux. Light curves are modeled via a double-Fermi empirical formulation:
$${\rm F}(t) = A_{0} \times \frac{1}{1 + \exp\left(\frac{A_{1}-t}{A_{2}}\right)} \times \frac{1}{1 + \exp\left(\frac{t-A_{3}}{A_{4}}\right)}$$\nResiduals are computed using $(O - C) = 0$ at cycle #31 (MJD 42409.9) with reference duration $20.5 \times P_{\rm orb} = 34.8534356\,\mathrm{d}$.

analysis.reason: FLITS is an open-source interactive workbench and pipeline tool for FRB dynamic spectrum analysis, DM optimization, polarization/RM synthesis, and model fitting (fitburst integration). While it is an astronomical software package rather than an observational discovery or theoretical breakthrough, it is directly useful for analyzing multi-telescope FRB data and checking dispersion and polarization properties.
analysis.result: FLITS unifies FRB data inspection, RFI mitigation, burst property extraction (signal-to-noise ratio, peak flux density, fluence, widths, and arrival times), burst-model fitting, and weighted RM synthesis ($Q, U, V$ polarization analysis) into reproducible JSON session states with checksum validation.
analysis.problem: FRB post-detection properties (DM, RM, scattering, sub-burst structure) depend heavily on subjective user choices (interference masking, background/burst region selection, time-frequency resolution), and automated DM optimization often fails or creates degeneracies with downward frequency drifting (the 'sad-trombone' effect) without interactive checks and reproducible session tracking.
analysis.method: The tool provides an interactive browser GUI and command-line interface (`flits measure`, `flits replay`). It supports multi-format data ingestion (SIGPROC filterbank, PSRFITS, CHIME/FRB HDF5), implements DM scoring metrics (S/N, `DM_phase` burst-structure, and smoothed-structure metric reporting DM uncertainty ranges), weighted RM synthesis ($P(\lambda^2) \propto \int F(\phi) e^{2i\phi\lambda^2} d\phi$), and integrated dynamic spectrum burst modeling based on `fitburst`.
limits: Instrumental polarization calibration and Earth ionospheric Faraday rotation corrections are not performed automatically and must be applied separately before RM analysis.
Reproducibility requires preserving the original raw data files and matching software execution environments alongside the JSON session metadata.

analysis.reason: This paper presents a computational proof of concept reformulating gamma-ray point source detection into a QUBO problem for simulated quantum annealing, without addressing transient astrophysics, compact object physics, or relativistic jets.
analysis.result: The QUBO framework correctly identifies the true candidate grid position in $97\%$ of the $500$ simulated AGILE maps (with remaining cases displaced by $0.5^{\circ}$). The source flux is recovered with a mean bias of $-1.9\%$ (standard deviation $8.3\%$), while the isotropic normalization is biased low by $-20.0\%$ (standard deviation $10.8\%$). The resulting detection significance $\sqrt{\mathrm{TS}}$ spans $17$ to $145$ (mean $65$) and correlates strongly with classical values (Pearson $r = 0.997$).
analysis.problem: Classical maximum-likelihood estimation for gamma-ray source detection and localization optimizes continuous parameters over Poisson counts $\ln L = \sum_{ij} n_{ij}\ln(\theta_{ij}) - \sum_{ij}\theta_{ij}$, which is non-polynomial and incompatible with Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) architectures.
analysis.method: The authors adopt a Gaussian approximation to map the Poisson log-likelihood to an unweighted least-squares objective $\chi^{2} = \|Rx - d\|^{2} = x^{T}Wx - 2V^{T}x + d\cdot d$, discretize continuous parameters $x = (g_{b}, c_{a})^{T}$ via a fixed-point binary expansion $x_{i} = \beta \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} 2^{k} q_{k}$ with $n=12$ bits, and implement position selection across $M = 81$ grid candidates with a one-hot penalty $\lambda (\sum_{m=1}^{M} z_{m} - 1)^{2}$ solved via simulated quantum annealing (SQA).
assumptions: A single point source is located at high Galactic latitude ($b = 30^{\circ}$) where Galactic diffuse emission $G_{ij}$ is negligible.
limits: The formulation is restricted to a single point source, exhibits a systematic $-20.0\%$ bias in background normalization, and requires minor-embedding qubit counts that currently exceed physical quantum hardware.

analysis.reason: The paper presents a quantitative gravitational self-lensing scenario in BH-NS binaries driven by Lense-Thirring precession to explain periodically repeating FRBs and pulse energy magnification. It derives critical constraints on intermediate-mass black hole (IMBH) companions and pulse delay timescales directly relevant to FRB burst morphology and environmental modeling.
analysis.result: Pure Keplerian self-lensing fails with a tiny activity window $\tau_{\mathrm{aw}}^{\mathrm{KP}} \sim \mathcal{O}(0.5\,\mathrm{hours})$, whereas Lense-Thirring precession with period $\tau_{\mathrm{LT}} = \frac{\pi(1-e^{2})^{3/2}c^{3}a^{3}}{G^{2}M_{\mathrm{BH}}^{2}\chi} = 2\tau_{\mathrm{FRB}}$ reproduces wide activity windows $\tau_{\mathrm{aw}}^{\mathrm{LT}} \sim 0.5\tau_{\mathrm{FRB}}$ for small inclinations $i \sim (5\text{--}8) \times 10^{-2}\,{^\circ}$. Splitting time delays $\tau_{\mathrm{lens}}^{\mathrm{Spl}} \approx \frac{4GM_{\mathrm{BH}}}{c^3}(1+z)\lambda(r_s/a)^{1/2} \sim 10^{-3}\text{--}10^{-2}\,\mathrm{s}$ match the observed millisecond waiting-time peak in FRB 20121102A, constraining the companion mass to $M_{\mathrm{BH}} \sim 10^3\text{--}10^4\,M_\odot$ with maximum amplification $\mathcal{A}_{\max} \approx \sqrt{8r_{s}a/R^{2}} \sim 10^4$ and gravitational wave merger timescale $\tau_{\mathrm{GW}} \sim 10^3\,\mathrm{yr}$.
analysis.problem: Periodically repeating Fast Radio Bursts (prFRBs) exhibit broad periodic activity windows ($30\%\text{--}50\%$ of their period) and pulse energies orders of magnitude higher than Galactic magnetars, which existing free-precession, stellar-wind eclipse, or simple orbital models struggle to simultaneously explain.
analysis.method: The authors construct a post-Newtonian binary dynamics and gravitational self-lensing framework using the Maeder-Liebes finite-source weak-field approximation $L_{\rm Lensed} = g^4 \mathcal{A} L_{\rm NS}$, incorporating Lense-Thirring and pericenter precession $\langle d\Omega/dt \rangle = \frac{2G^2 M_{\rm BH}^2}{c^3 a^3 (1-e^2)^{3/2}} \chi$, relativistic timing delays (Rømer, Einstein, and Shapiro), and Monte Carlo simulations of magnetar-like log-normal pulse distributions.
assumptions: The radio emitter is a neutron star (or magnetar) in a close orbit around a rotating black hole, periodically emitting pulses with an intrinsic log-normal energy distribution.
limits: Standard Galactic magnetar intrinsic pulse energies ($10^{29}\text{--}10^{30}\,\mathrm{erg}$) require either an intrinsically brighter emitter ($\sim 10^{34}\,\mathrm{erg}$) or extremely small emission radii to reach the highest FRB energetics through weak lensing.

The population rate is highly constrained by the edge-on geometric alignment fraction $f_{\rm geom} \sim 10^{-3}$ and tight binary formation fractions, yielding $N_{\rm obs} \lesssim 1$, meaning this mechanism can only account for a rare subset of prFRBs rather than the broader FRB population.

source_sections: Coherent Radio Emission from Flux Rope Mergers in 3D Relativistic Reconnection

analysis.reason: This work presents 3D PIC simulations of coherent radio emission from flux rope mergers in relativistic reconnection with outflow boundary conditions and guide fields, directly testing FRB and pulsar emission engine models.
analysis.result: Coherent fast magnetosonic waves are stably excited via flux rope mergers in 3D relativistic reconnection, yielding a radiation efficiency of $\eta \sim 7 \times 10^{-4}$ for $B_g/B_0 = 0$ and $\eta \sim (1\text{--}2) \times 10^{-3}$ for moderate guide fields ($B_g/B_0 = 0.1\text{--}0.3$). The escaping radiation is 100% linearly polarized X-mode ($\,\delta\bm{E}\perp\bm{B}$), with a polarization angle offset between opposite sides of the sheet of $\Delta\mathrm{PA} \sim 2\arctan(B_g/B_0)$.
analysis.problem: Whether 3D relativistic instabilities (e.g., relativistic drift kink instability and flux rope kink instability) and realistic outflow boundaries suppress coherent radio wave emission found in simplified 2D periodic relativistic reconnection simulations.
analysis.method: 3D particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations of pair plasmas using TRISTAN-MP with open outflow boundaries along $x$ ($L_x=1600\,c/\omega_p$, $L_z=816\,c/\omega_p$), cold magnetization $\sigma = B_0^2/(4\pi n_0 m c^2) = 10$, and guide fields $B_g/B_0 \in \{0, 0.1, 0.3\}$, diagnosing wave Poynting flux $S_{\mathrm{wave}}=(c/4\pi)(\delta E_{z}\delta B_{x}-\delta E_{x}\delta B_{z})$ and efficiency $\eta \equiv S_{\mathrm{wave}}/S_0$.
citation_leads: Coherent Radio Emission from Flux Rope Mergers in 3D Relativistic Reconnection: “We find $\eta\sim 7\times 10^{-4}$ without a guide field, a factor of a few below 2D results, and $\eta\sim(1\text{--}2)\times 10^{-3}$ at moderate guide fields, comparable to 2D with no guide field.”
III.1 Efficiency: “The efficiency of converting inflowing Poynting flux into outgoing coherent waves is thus”

III.3 Polarization angle: “In all our simulations, we find that these waves are linearly polarized X-mode waves (i.e., with $\delta\bm{E}\perp\bm{B}$), which, as we will show below, sets their polarization angle directly.”

IV Summary and Observational Implications: “In the presence of a guide field, waves escaping from opposite sides of the sheet therefore differ in PA by $\Delta\mathrm{PA}\sim 2\,\arctan(B_{g}/B_{0})$.”
analysis.research_progress: Demonstrates that 3D kinetic reconnection maintains high coherent emission efficiency $\eta \sim (1\text{--}2)\times 10^{-3}$ through interlocked flux rope structures, confirming reconnection as a viable coherent radio mechanism for FRBs and pulsar nanoshots.

figures.caption: Figure 4: Large-scale, coherent structures in the $B_{g}/B_{0}=0.3$ simulation at $ct/L=6.75$. Top row: Volume rendering of the average particle outflow velocity $\langle v_{x}\rangle/c$. Purple and red field lines show the upstream field above and below the sheet, respectively, and the tubes on each side of the sheet follow the corresponding field direction. The left panels zoom in on the interface between a tube above and a tube below the sheet, with a sample of reconnected field lines overlaid. The green and gold field lines originate from two different diffusion regions (shown in black, i.e., regions of strong $E_{\parallel})$, and are pulled in opposite directions along $x$. Both of these bundles of field lines cross the sheet, with one end above it and one end below it. Bottom row: Same as above, but showing particle density. The linkage point between the two bundles appears in the left-hand zoom-in as a large overdense region. The diffusion region that produced the green bundle is indicated by a black-outlined arrow, while a newly created flux rope is indicated by a purple-outlined arrow. A green bar indicates that the density structure is $\sim 200\,c/\omega_{p}$ wide.
figures.label: Fig. 4
figures.physical_core: The figure shows how reconnected field bundles from different diffusion regions are pulled in opposite directions along $x$, link across the current sheet, and form a large overdense structure. It illustrates the proposed physical picture for transporting reconnected field away from the diffusion regions in 3D.

figures.caption: Figure 5: Polarization angle (PA) of the outgoing waves, for $B_{g}/B_{0}=0$ (top row) and $B_{g}/B_{0}=0.3$ (bottom row), at $ct/L=5.6$. The four plots show $x$ – $z$ slices near the top of the box (left column) and bottom of the box (right column), $\sim 640\,c/\omega_{p}$ from the current sheet, showing the outgoing Poynting flux carried by the coherent waves, normalized by the inflowing flux $S_{0}$. The yellow-purple areas are patches of high-intensity waves. The light blue ticks denote the direction of the oscillating electric vector in these bright patches, whose angle from the $z$ axis is the PA. In the $B_{g}/B_{0}=0$ case, the waves escaping on either side of the box have their electric field aligned with the $z$ axis. For the $B_{g}/B_{0}=0.3$ case, on the other hand, because the PA of the outgoing waves is set by the direction of the upstream field, there is a rotation across the sheet by $\Delta\mathrm{PA}\sim 2\,\arctan(B_{g}/B_{0})$.
figures.label: Fig. 5
figures.physical_core: The simulated outgoing coherent waves are linearly polarized. Their polarization angle follows the upstream field direction; for $B_g/B_0=0.3$, the predicted rotation between waves escaping from opposite sides is $\Delta\mathrm{PA}\sim 2\arctan(B_g/B_0)$.

analysis.result: Detections in the $0.5-10\ \mathrm{keV}$ range reveal quiescent X-ray luminosities spanning $L_{\mathrm{X}} \sim 10^{33}-10^{36}\ \mathrm{erg\ s^{-1}}$, with photon indices $\Gamma \sim 0.5-2.0$ and blackbody temperatures $kT_{\rm bb} \sim 0.8-1.6\ \mathrm{keV}$ from emitting radii $R \sim 0.1-2\ \mathrm{km}$. A power-law correlation connects X-ray luminosity and emission radius as $L \propto R^{\alpha}$ with index $\alpha = 2.3 \pm 0.2$. In addition, upper limits on non-detected sources (e.g. 2S 1553$-$542 and RX J0812.4$-$3114) fall below the theoretical propeller luminosity $L_{\rm prop} \simeq 4\times 10^{37}k^{7/2}B_{12}^{2}P^{-7/3}M_{1.4}^{-2/3}R_{6}^{5}\ \mathrm{erg\ s^{-1}}$, confirming propeller or cold disc inhibition.

analysis.method: Analysis of SRG/eROSITA eRASS1 survey data ($0.2-8\ \mathrm{keV}$) using Cash statistics and Akaike Information Criterion ($\mathrm{AIC} = 2k + C$) in XSPEC to fit absorbed power-law (`tbabs*powerlaw`) and absorbed blackbody (`tbabs*bbodyrad`) models, compared against theoretical thresholds for propeller transitions ($L_{\rm prop}$) and cold disk accretion ($L_{\rm cold}$).

analysis.reason: The paper provides a comprehensive 17.9-year Fermi-LAT timing and spectral analysis of changing-look blazars, demonstrating that their relativistic jet variability and central engine Eddington ratios consistently mimic FSRQs rather than BL Lacs.
analysis.result: Changing-look blazars (CLBs) exhibit fractional variability $F_{\rm var} = 0.483$ at a 30-day cadence that is statistically indistinguishable from FSRQs ($0.437$, $p=0.94$) but significantly higher than BL Lacs ($0.262$, $p=1.4\times 10^{-4}$). analysis.result: Nuclear electric dipole polarizability constraints (CNSP-4 set) reduce the spread in the surface–ISCO transition gravitational mass $M_{\rm tr}(f)$ and equatorial radius $R_{\rm eq}$ across spin frequencies $f$ by factors of $7$--$10$ ($85$--$90\%$ reduction), bringing mass uncertainty below $0.025\,M_{\odot}$ and radius uncertainty below $0.15\text{ km}$. Along the transition, the disk inner-edge Keplerian orbital frequency $\nu_{\rm in} = \Omega_{\rm orb}(R_{\rm in})/(2\pi)$ is confined to a band narrower than $20\text{ Hz}$ (down from $38$--$134\text{ Hz}$ across the full DD–PC family). analysis.problem: Uncertainties in the nuclear equation of state—especially the density dependence of the nuclear symmetry energy—heavily blur theoretical predictions of whether a neutron star's accretion disk inner edge is truncated by the physical stellar surface ($R_{\rm in} = R_{\rm eq}$) or an external ISCO ($R_{\rm in} = R_{\rm ISCO} > R_{\rm eq}$), hampering the use of kHz QPOs to infer neutron star masses and radii.

analysis.result: Standard ECSN models with dusty winds cannot simultaneously reproduce the light curves and colors of ILRTs: the intrinsic drop in input luminosity after the plateau causes $r_{\rm sub} \propto L_{\rm input}^{1/2}$ to shrink, triggering a runaway increase in optical depth $\tau_V$ and causing the optical luminosity to plummet by orders of magnitude; attempting to flatten the decline using dense CSM shock interaction ($L_{s,\rm rad} \propto t^{-0.3}$) requires $\dot{M}_{\rm dense} \simeq 9.7 \times 10^{-3}\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$ and produces excessively red post-plateau colors ($B - V > 4$) that contradict observed ILRT colors ($B - V \lesssim 1.2\text{--}1.6$).
analysis.problem: Theoretical ECSN models from super-AGB progenitors predict plateau luminosities ($10^{41}\text{--}10^{42}\text{ erg s}^{-1}$) and post-plateau drops that are too luminous and steep compared to smooth, low-luminosity ILRTs like SN 2008S and NGC 300-OT.
analysis.method: The authors develop a semi-analytical radiative transfer framework coupling ECSN light curves with Chevalier-type shock interaction luminosity ($L_s(t) \simeq \frac{1}{2}\dot{M} v_s^3 / v_w \propto t^{-0.3}$), amorphous carbon dust grain growth limited by gas recombination and growth timescales ($f_{\rm dust}(r,t)$), dynamic dust sublimation ($r_{\rm sub} \propto L_{\rm input}^{1/2}$), and light-travel time boxcar smoothing ($2R/c$).

analysis.reason: The paper leverages the FRB DM-redshift relation and kSZ measurements to break the baryon-magnetic field degeneracy in RM stacks, obtaining magnetization and plasma beta constraints in galaxy groups and clusters.
analysis.result: For a coherence length $l_c = 10\,\mathrm{kpc}$ within $R < R_{200c}$, the 95% upper limits on the line-of-sight rms magnetic field are $B_{\parallel,\mathrm{rms}} < 3.9\text{--}11.6\,\mu\mathrm{G}$ for DESI BGS groups and $< 2.3\text{--}6.4\,\mu\mathrm{G}$ for RASS clusters, scaling as $l_c^{-1/2}$; the 95% lower limits on plasma beta are $\beta > 0.31$ and $\beta > 11$ respectively, derived via $B_{\parallel,\mathrm{rms}}(R)=B_{\parallel,\mathrm{eff}}(R)\sqrt{L(R)/l_c}$ with $B_{\parallel,\mathrm{eff}}(R)=\mathrm{RM}_{\mathrm{rest}}(R)/[0.812\,\mathrm{DM}(R)]\,\mu\mathrm{G}$.
analysis.problem: Disentangling the severe baryon-magnetic field degeneracy in Faraday rotation measure (RM), which integrates $n_e B_\parallel$, and circumventing sign cancellations to measure the magnetic field profiles and plasma $\beta$ in galaxy groups and clusters.
analysis.method: Cross-correlating $\mathrm{RM}^2$ from SPICE-RACS DR2 with foreground tracers (DESI BGS groups and RASS clusters), dividing by electron column density profiles from joint FRB DM–$z$ and ACT kSZ calibrations ($N_e(R)=\tau(R)/\sigma_T$), and scaling by chord length $L(R)=2\sqrt{(2R_{200c})^2-R^2}$ under coherence length $l_c$ via $B_{\parallel,\mathrm{rms}}(R)=B_{\parallel,\mathrm{eff}}(R)\sqrt{L(R)/l_{c}}$.

analysis.result: The authors derive the exact bivariate differential rate distribution (DRD) for velocity kicks in isotropic clusters, yielding closed-form DRD solutions for King models and nuclear star clusters (NSCs) with $\rho \propto r^{-\gamma}$. For extreme-eccentricity orbits ($1-e \ll 1$) in NSCs, strong scatterings at apocenter can impart angular momentum jumps $\Delta J \approx J_c - J$ (where $J_c^5 = \frac{85}{3} \frac{k \sigma(a)^3}{n(a) \langle M_{\rm s}^2 \rangle \ln\Lambda} \frac{G^{7/2} M_\bullet^{9/2} M}{a^{3/2} c^5}$), ejecting compact objects back into the two-body relaxation regime and canceling EMRIs with a scale-invariant rate $N_{\rm CE} \sim \Gamma_{{\rm CE},o} t_{\rm GW} \propto a^0$. The orbit-averaged stellar ejection rate near pericenter scales as $\langle \Gamma_{\rm ej} \rangle \approx \frac{16\pi}{5 P (\gamma-1)} \frac{M_{\rm s}}{M_\bullet^2} r_{\rm inf}^\gamma \rho_{\rm inf} a^{3-\gamma} (1-e)^{1-\gamma}$.
analysis.problem: Standard cluster evolution and loss-cone dynamics rely on low-order diffusion coefficients from weak small-angle scatterings, which fail to capture rare, non-diffusive phase-space jumps caused by strong gravitational scatterings that can eject stars or disrupt extreme mass ratio inspirals (EMRIs).
analysis.method: Analytical formulation of hyperbolic encounters in spherical isotropic star clusters by projecting velocity kicks into parallel and perpendicular components ($\Delta v_{||}, \Delta v_\perp$), transforming the kick distribution into a two-dimensional planar slice integral over field star distribution functions $f(v_f)$: $\frac{\mathrm{d}^2\Gamma}{\mathrm{d}\Delta v_{||} \mathrm{d}\Delta v_{\perp} } = 8\pi G^2 M_{\rm s}^2 \frac{\Delta v_{\perp}}{(\Delta v_{||}^2 + \Delta v_{\perp}^2)^{5/2}} \int_{\Delta \hat{v}\cdot \vec{v}_f = \kappa} f(v_f)\, \mathrm{d}A$, mapping to action space $(E, J)$ via pericenter radial approximation, and orbit-averaging scattering rates.

However, one can hypothesize that although AM diffusion appears to be subdominant, there is still a rare chance of a close”

The top panel shows $\gamma=3/2$, the middle displays the Bahcall-Wolf solution of $\gamma=7/4$, and the bottom panel shows $\gamma=2$. opening_brief.intro: Featured reading: "Discovery of a New Electron Spectrum Produced by Fast Cooling of Relativistic Electrons" and 26 other key developments.

focus_paper.title: Discovery of a New Electron Spectrum Produced by Fast Cooling of Relativistic Electrons

must_read.label: Discovery of a New Electron Spectrum Produced by Fast Cooling of Relativistic Electrons
must_read.text: In the fast-cooling regime below the minimum injection Lorentz factor ($\gamma_e < \gamma_m$), the time-evolving cooled electron spectrum follows the smooth broken power-law form $f_{\rm U}(\gamma_e,t) = A(t) \gamma_e^{-2} [1 + \gamma_0(t)/\gamma_e]^{-\beta}$, scaling asymptotically as $\gamma_e^{-2}$ for $\gamma_e \gg \gamma_0(t)$ and $\gamma_e^{-2+\beta}$ for $\gamma_e \ll \gamma_0(t)$.

must_read.label: Coherent Radio Emission from Flux Rope Mergers in 3D Relativistic Reconnection
must_read.text: Coherent fast magnetosonic waves are stably excited via flux rope mergers in 3D relativistic reconnection, yielding a radiation efficiency of $\eta \sim 7 \times 10^{-4}$ for $B_g/B_0 = 0$ and $\eta \sim (1\text{--}2) \times 10^{-3}$ for moderate guide fields ($B_g/B_0 = 0.1\text{--}0.3$).

key_highlights.title: An intermediate-mass stripped star with a dark companion in the Small Magellanic Cloud
key_highlights.result: The binary has an orbital period of $P_{\rm orb} = 19.95 \pm 0.002\,{\rm hr}$ ($19.947 \pm 0.002\,{\rm hr}$), radial velocity semi-amplitude $K = 91.7^{+3.2}_{-3.1}\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}}$, and eccentricity $e = 0.032^{+0.031}_{-0.022}$, yielding a binary mass function $f_m \approx 0.066\,M_\odot$.

key_highlights.title: CROMA: a GPU-accelerated Fokker--Planck solver for modeling non-thermal emission in post-processing cosmological simulations
key_highlights.result: CROMA implements an implicit Chang-Cooper scheme solved via Parallel Cyclic Reduction (PCR) on GPUs, achieving a tridiagonal solve throughput saturating at $R_{\rm solve} \approx 10^{3}\ \mathrm{tracers\ s^{-1}}$ per MPI task, an end-to-end wall-clock throughput of $R_{\rm wall} \approx 400\ \mathrm{tracers\ s^{-1}}$ per task at $N_{\rm trc} \sim 10^6$ ($N_{\rm bin} = 128$), an acceleration factor of $\sim 10\times$ compared to 32 CPU cores, and a synchrotron emissivity computation speedup by a factor of $N_\theta \approx 10^3$ using precomputed tables.
